text: The development of the UAV field is changing with each passing day, especially a lot of research has been done on the road of autonomous and controllable. At present, the control module has become the mainstream design. Because it can perform high-performance real-time image processing, which is popular, but this design has the disadvantages of high power consumption, slow processing and low response speed. With its high-performance concurrent computing mode, FPGA has excellent performance in signal processing, graphics deduction, control and other fields, and has low power consumption. The embedded architecture on the edge side has attracted more and more attention. Small UAVs have limitations such as small size, low power load, and high timeliness. The GPU-ARM architecture cannot meet the requirements of small drones. In order to solve the above problems, this paper proposes a new UAV architecture based on FPGA-ARM-GPU for the use of small UAV.

In the current UAV market, GPU which is dominant image computing center dominates the main strea-m. Especially NVIDIA Jetson series is the main core single board [1], with Pixhawk 4 flight control module. Among them, Jetson is the core of image processing, signal transmission, and data processing. Pix4 is based on its own sensors, L3GD20H gyroscope, LSM303D accelerometer and MS5611 barometer [2]. The data is returned to its internal STM32 for calculating to control the drone. The Px4 flight controller and GPU board become the core of the drone through hardware connection. The software architecture directly enables ROS to communicate and connect.

However, the miniaturization of UAV has become an important trend in both the commercial and military fields. But at the same time it brings many problems and limitations. The first is the limitation of the size and weight of the UAV. The distance between the two blades of the small drone is generally 30 to 40cm, and the total weight is controlled at about 2kg, minus the rack, battery and camera part, leaving the weight at the core. About 400g, if you follow the previous GPU+PX4 plan, the total weight is 300g. The weight of the cable and plug is obviously beyond the standard.

The second is energy efficiency. After miniaturization of UAV, redundant sensors will be removed. Generally, surrounding cameras, accelerometers and gyroscopes are only retained. Among them, image processing capabilities are the most important. We can see in this paper [3], only simple image operations are processed. The input and output GPU has high efficiency, but as the operation becomes more complex. When image filtering, image analysis, and image geometric transformation are required, the energy efficiency of FPGA is more than 2 times that of GPU. When small UAVs only use the camera, the above complex algorithm operations will all be used. In terms of energy efficiency, FPGA is better. The last is integration. Small drones require a highly integrated design architecture. In the previous scheme, flight control data, image data, and communication are controlled by two independent ARM cores. Cortex M4 controls the corresponding data of the flight control sensor. Cortex A9 controls the image data and other configurations, which results in a waste of computing resources. In terms of image data processing capabilities [4], in the same Bpp, processing 32-bit displayed images, the processing speed of A9 can reach 24.2 Megapixels per second, but the processing power of M4 is only 5.68 million pixels per second, which is only 1/5 of the former. In response to the above three issues, this article proposes an FPGA-based UAV heterogeneous computing platform. and can intelligently allocate the required resources for the corresponding calculations for the data types.

The main contributions of this article are:

A new highly integrated core architecture of UAV flight control computing.

With the deepening of research and development in the field of UAV, the computing core has become the focus of current research.

Professor Erwan Moréac of Université Bretagne University [5] proposed a ROS-based FPGA simulation system, which comprehensively demonstrated the model simulation method of FPGA in the middle of UAV.

Brennan Cain [6] of the University of Southern California proposed to design an open-source drone comput-ing architecture based on PYNQ, which simplifies the threshold for getting started with FPGAs and proposes various practical IP cores to make it more convenient to conduct corresponding research. Using Python to write FPGA IP cores can remove the problem of high hardware description language thresholds. However, the study did not involve autonomy. Only a set of FPGA combined with UAV theory is proposed. There are still shortcomings in the need to combine autonomy and intelligence, and the research only relies on FPGA for calculations. In this regard, more in-depth research can be carried out. This paper by University of Science and Technology of China [7] combines FPGA with Pixhawk and proposes an optimization method for flight data. The research points out that FPGA has a strong filtering and de-noising ability in heterogeneous platforms. FPGA is well integrated into UAV flight control, showing a UAV based on FPGA with heterogeneous platform computing architecture. But it fails to fully demonstrate the combination of FPGA and UAV in image and artificial intelligence ability.

From these papers, it can be seen that the heterogeneous computing architecture with FPGA as the computing core and UAV are more and more closely integrated. Because of its highly parallelized streaming computing architecture, FPGA has obvious advantages in processing image data and mass data. However, when autonomous UAVs rely solely on the camera as the only way to perceive the outside world, complex image processing capabilities are the main con-sideration for the computing architecture.

From these two papers by Laszlo Schaffer [8] of the University of Szeged and Seungsik Moon [9] of Pohang University of Science and Technology, whether using CNN or PCA algorithms for image recognition or image training and deduction, FPGAs are becoming more and more popular as the core of image processing.

At present, FPGAs are still used for image processing in the UAV field. GPU is still the main computing core. FPGA-ARM heterogeneous computing UAV platforms are few. Some research can refer to autonomous vehicles. And visual image data is also used as an example. The main core computing, the architecture research of the University of Illinois [10] is a heterogeneous computing platform based on FPGA+GPU, using FPGA as the core of the monitoring task, GPU as the core of the driving task, and FPGA as the auxiliary filing of the GPU. When the GPU appears an error occurs, FPGA can be used as a substitute for the core to perform calculations. This architectural idea can be used in the UAV autonomous flight architecture.

On the basis of the above three aspects of research, the research of UAV computing architecture should be towards the direction of FPGA heterogeneous intelligent computing architecture. This article also proposes a novel architecture and implementation based on this direction.

The new architecture direction studied in this paper is to add FPGA to the original ARM-GPU to assist in data processing. We split the design of the Pix flight controller, and reintegrate it with the new heterogeneous computing platform. FPGA is as a data intelligent transfer and the core of acceleration. On this basis, the GPU only processes simple images. The ARM core data calculation function is replaced by FPGA, which reduces the work of ARM and provides calculation space for the transplantation of flight controllers. Based on this, this chapter will introduce in detail.

The FPGA and Arm core in this paper is XCZ7020 and Cortex-A9,like Figure 1.An external Nvidia GPU board constitutes a whole core computing structure. The Pix4 flight control is separated separately and does not use the original built-in. The core of Cortex-M4 only retains its original sensor module, and connects the camera. The rest of the wireless communication module, motor drive module, and numerical control module are all controlled by ARM. The overall architecture is shown in Fig. 2.

The most important communication problem for heterogeneous computing platforms is that FPGA, GPU, and ARM are different structures. They cannot be controlled by the same kind of bus. Therefore, different buses must be designed for different chips.

The first is between FPGA and ARM. We use the AXI [11] bus protocol, which is the high-speed bus in the AMBA protocol. It mainly transmits sensor data which has been processed by the FPGA except for the image. The sensor data must be removed by the FPGA to reduce weight, fit.

ARM can directly use the processed data, and the data processing algorithm does not need to be written in ARM, which can save corresponding computing resources for processing additional data.

The second is the communication between FPGA and GPU. In traditional data transmission, because both are PCIE control devices, ARM is required to transfer data. But this causes a higher delay and data loss. In the case of high immediacy requirements, it cannot be met. So new com-munication methods are needed.

Data communication is mainly to read and write registers in RAM, but GPU still belongs to von Neumann architecture. So it needs instruction set to run and needs shared memory for caching, while FPGA is based on the existing for the logic is directly controlled. If you want to consider the sending and receiving issues at the same time, there will be too many considerations. Considering UAV usage only involves GPU fetching graphics data from FPGA, and FPGA does not need to fetch data from GPU.

Finally, the communication of each sensor, acceleration, gyroscope and other data sensors are connected to the ARM through I2C.Each sensor is controlled by ARM. The sensor data is connected by the SPI bus to the FPGA. The data will be processed by the FPGA before being processed. Handed over to ARM for use.

In Figure 3,you can see the whole design of IP in FPGA.

Sensor core: Based on an independent IP core, used at the same stage of the data path. The inertial measurement unit sensor IP core is used to configure and collect data the inertial measurement unit of the body itself. The core uses the AXI IIC bus interface to communicate with the sensor through the I2C protocol, which is configured to receive the correct data in a format that we can use.Then it reads the value from the Sensor after the correct configuration. The data is converted into 16-bit fixed-width integer values representing the current yaw, pitch, roll and height.Then it can be sent to other IP cores for normalization and processing. The data can also be configured for attitude or speed mode. The other part is the image sensor unit processor IP core, which controls and transmits data through the MIPI interface and I2C.It converts the data of multiple cameras into fixed-width values for subsequent processing.

Identify core: This part is mainly for data screening and classification of posture data and image data. It mainly involves data recognition and judgment, enabling different acceleration kernels for different data, and distributing the data. Currently, only two types of data are involved. The function of the core is small. When multiple types of data are involved, this core will serve as the processing core of the architecture.

Accelerate core: After the data received from the sensor core is transmitted to the core, the core is designed as a screening and discrimination algorithm based on integral calculation. The screening and discrimination algorithm is mainly suitable for inertial posture data, removing and supplementing bad data from the data obtained by the Sensor core. The image acceleration algorithm is mainly designed for the fusion and compression of multiple cameras. The single-frame patterns collected by a singlecamera are spliced into a full-frame for further processing and subsequent processing. Please see Fig. 4 for specific design. Fig. 4 is the main part of the overall circuit. Control core: The core is designed as a proportional integral derivative controller, which is a general closed-loop control algorithm. Here, we use the target value obtained from the remote control receiver, the measured value obtained from the sensor and our PID constants to calculate the estimated roll and pitch values, which we can send to the motor for execution. Using this IP core, we try to stabilize our roll and pitch during flight; proportional integral derivative helps to consider the proportional difference, cumulative error and rate of change to ensure that we will not exceed the target value. For yaw and thrust, the controller is fully proportional, and this is taken into account during the mixing process. The mixing is done in this core, and our output data is prepared into six fixed-point duty cycle outputs.

As the core of the FPGA, the above related cores need to be hardened on the FPGA. You can use HLS to design or directly use VerilogHDL to write. ARM will eventually only be used as a control module that controls the activation of the core to reduce the amount of calcula-tions on ARM. The amount of calculation is distributed.

The GPU in the organization in this article is mainly the process of inference. The training model uses the human form model that has been trained on the server. Therefore, the GPU involves two technical points. One is the selection of the human pose model, and the other is mainly resolution of communication problems between GPU and FPGA.The connection of three part is shown in Figure 5.

The UAV architecture in this article only uses the camera for external perception. When identifying the task target, it is often externally scanned at a depression angle. Therefore, a single face training model cannot carry all tasks, so the overall posture of the target needs to be selected. model.

The current mainstream human pose models include DensePose,OpenPose,Realtime,MultiPersonPoseEstimation, AlphaPose,HumanBodyPose,and DeepPose.Considering the carrier and response time, the OpenPose model is our primary consideration model, but this model need to use high-speed memory and high-speed clock.So the weight of the compression algorithm is needed to further reduce the storage space.Here we need to learn from a set of optimization algorithms of Tokyo Institute of Technology to meet our requirements [12].

The communication problem with FPGA is the most important problem in GPU design. Generally, GPU is controlled by ARM and communicates directly through PCIE interface. If GPU wants to communicate with FPGA, the general method is to convert by ARM. In this case, communication is in progress. There is one more conversion step, that is, ARM reads the GPU data and then distributes it to the FPGA, which increases the communication delay. Therefore, direct communication between the GPU and the FPGA is required to remove the ARM transfer.

Although Nvdia provides the GPUDirect RDMA interface, this interface cannot be used on consumer GPUs, so a new ending solution is needed. Refer to the paper [13], it can be seen that it is a communication method based on PCIE Switch.

In the architecture of this article, it is mainly GPU reading, regardless of two-way operation, that is, let FPGA as Slave, GPU as Master, FPGA memory is mapped to PCIE bus, GPU uses the existing API interface in CUDA to allocate a physical address, And directly manipulate the virtual address of the FPGA, so that you can directly access the memory of the FPGA to allow the GPU to read and write. Through the above method, you can simply perform one-way data transmission between the GPU and the FPGA to ensure the stability of the image data.
We designed and made the UAV according to this paper.Next, we will introduce several parts of our UAV. The picture in Figure 6 is our material object of UAV.

This part involves the transmission of control information. We use AT9S as the radio frequency remote control, R9DS 9 channel as the receiver.Then we use the SUBS channel as the connection channel. This way, the mode can be switched on the remote control because it is connected if PWM is used. Each channel needs to be wired, and the PWM signal uses the high level time as the control signal, the level edge is easily disturbed, causing erroneous control, and the PX4 original flight control architecture is equipped with SUBS Driven, so it is directly connected to the corresponding setting interface.

The core of the UAV architecture is the main control part. For FPGA and ARM, we directly use the Xilinx ZYNQ7020 main control board.We uses only the GPU core of the JETSON AGX XAVIER, and removes the CPU part of its ARM v8.

The sensor is mainly composed of two parts, one part is an inertial attitude sensor.Among them, the barometric altimeter uses MS5611,the inertial sensor uses MPU6000 module,and the six-axis sensor module is composed of three-axis accelerometer and three-axis gyroscope.In figure 7,two pcb board connect with main board according to I2C.This is our design of sensor module.

The other part is the camera module, which uses a total of 8 cameras with a front, rear, left, and right binocular design, and a Structure Core depth camera for the binocular. The front attitude sensor collects information such as the flight attitude, speed, and altitude of the UAV. The camera is responsible for receiving the surrounding environment, detecting obstacles, and judging the target.

The attitude sensor is connected through SCL and SDA on the ZYNQ single board, using 3.3V power supply, and finally connected to the AXI I2C IP. The camera is directly connected using USB-A, and the data and clock lines of I2C and I2S are also connected to the PL end of the board.

The UAV designed in this article is a quad-rotor UAV, and the frame uses DJI S450 and 3508 motors. The reason for the selection is the relatively mature overall body structure, which is relatively light and can provide sufficient lift, because The design itself is light-weighted as the standard, and the weight will be reduced in the future, so only the maximum lift of 2KG is required.

First of all, the main goal is to complete the integrated design. We can design our own PCB board which packages the attitude sensor and the main control chip together, and completely integrate the main control chip, instead of using the fly as it is now. Wires connect different boards to achieve a high level of integration and make it a whole.

The second is in the direction of FPGA. At present, since there are few types of sensor data, filters are used to process the identification IP, that is to say, it is only necessary to determine whether it is inertial sensor data, and it is not directly distributed to the graphics processing IP core. In this way, the purpose of intelligently identifying data as expected at the beginning is not achieved. Different IP checks can be allocated to process the data according to different types of data. Therefore, the identification of IP cores needs to be improved. This expectation is a reference Finally, there is the combination of GPU and FPGA. As research progresses, more and more FPGAs have replaced GPUs to achieve graphics deduction results. We are also considering completely removing GPUs and making FPGAs as the core of graphics calculations. You can see that FPGAs are used instead of GPUs. It is entirely possible. The advantage of GPU in floating-point operations and simple operations require FPGAs to find ways to replace them, such as multi-block FPGA coordination, internal core redistribution and other technologies to achieve, such a heterogeneous architecture can make small unmanned. The machine goes further.

The purpose of this paper is to demonstrate a new drone architecture and we discuss the practical application of heterogeneous platforms. This article provides a general overview of our team's current research on heterogeneous UAVs. With FPGA and ARM as the core, GPU as the assistance core, we integrated PX4 flight control to form an integrated embedded computing core. Further research will be carried out later. Finally, it can realize the FPGA-ARM dualcore low-power, high-performance embedded computing platform, and realize the miniaturization and intelligence of UAVs.

Of course, there are still many extensions to the application of FPGA in drones. This article only studies a small part, and hopes to provide an idea for the following researchers, which can be used in drones and even embedded fields. Far, not only limited to a single computing architecture idea, fully understand and give full play to the advantages of different types of architecture.
